name: USGS Pikes Peak, 1:125,000, 1894
basis: Reprojected from the USGS GeoTIFF (Pikes_Peak_234096_1894_125000.tif). One NAD27 shift for the whole district. Not checked against the ground at this place. Checked at Cameron against the 1 m lidar: the 1894 sheet has no railway here; it names Grassy Gulch, running from the head of the flat east to the creek.

fit.note: as published; the year is the edition in the file name, not the survey

name: USGS Pikes Peak, 1:125,000, edition of 1901 (reprinted 1909)
basis: Cut from the USGS scan (Pikes_Peak_402404_1901_62500.tif), placed by the sheet's four corner marks because the file's own georeference is wrong. One NAD27 shift for the whole district. Not checked against the ground at this place. Checked at Cameron against the 1 m lidar: the 1901 sheet draws the top of the Midland Terminal's loop within about 200 ft of the bank on the ground, but the line leaving the loop to the south-east about 500 ft east of the OpenStreetMap trace (that ground is under mine dumps and could not be checked). It draws one railway through the flat, with a second coming in from the east and stopping about 1.9 miles east of the loop, and it does not print the name Cameron.

fit.note: as published; the year is the edition in the file name, not the survey
